answer_text:
Let the parameter of interest be

\[
\theta=\log \sigma,
\qquad \sigma=e^\theta.
\]

Since \(X_1,\dots,X_n\) are i.i.d. \(N(0,\sigma^2)\), the joint density is

\[
f(x_1,\dots,x_n\mid \theta)
=
(2\pi)^{-n/2} e^{-n\theta}
\exp\!\left\{-\frac{e^{-2\theta}}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2\right\}.
\]

The log-likelihood is

\[
\ell(\theta)
=
\text{constant}
-n\theta
-\frac{e^{-2\theta}}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^2.
\]

Differentiate with respect to \(\theta\):

\[
\frac{\partial \ell}{\partial \theta}
=
-n+e^{-2\theta}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^2.
\]

Differentiate again:

\[
\frac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \theta^2}
=
-2e^{-2\theta}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^2.
\]

Thus the Fisher information for \(\theta\) in the full sample is

\[
I_n(\theta)
=
-\mathbb{E}_\theta\!\left[\frac{\partial^2 \ell}{\partial \theta^2}\right]
=
2e^{-2\theta}\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E}_\theta[X_i^2].
\]

Since \(X_i\sim N(0,e^{2\theta})\), we have

\[
\mathbb{E}_\theta[X_i^2]=e^{2\theta}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
I_n(\theta)=2e^{-2\theta}\cdot n e^{2\theta}=2n.
\]

By the Cramér-Rao lower bound, for any unbiased estimator \(T\) of \(\log\sigma\),

\[
\operatorname{Var}_\theta(T)
\ge
\frac{\left(\frac{d}{d\theta}\log\sigma\right)^2}{I_n(\theta)}
=
\frac{1}{2n}.
\]

Hence the Cramér-Rao lower bound is

\[
\boxed{\frac{1}{2n}}.
\]
